title: Read ordered vendor suggestions offline without creating Vendor identity or write authority

requirements.invariant: Vendor/source evidence remains a captured value on its owning Item, Expense or Transaction. Reading or selecting a reusable suggestion cannot create accounting activity, change money, or replace the owning record's source snapshot.

Vendor suggestions are Account-scoped ordered reference entries with stable identity, preserved display spelling, explicit lifecycle and revision, and deterministic order. A suggestion remains convenience data rather than canonical Vendor or historical accounting identity.

Each visible entry has stable VendorSuggestionID, exact AccountID, bounded display value, normalized comparison key, active or archived lifecycle, unique presentation order and revision. Selection yields only the preserved free-text source value and never a Vendor relationship.

requirements.section: Clients, Projects, notes, preferences, and reference data
requirements.invariant: One narrow backend-neutral VendorSuggestionQuerying port streams already-authorized local snapshots for exactly one Account. Read access is separate from O-026 mutation capability and carries no role, credential, backend path, generic CRUD or writer method.

The local result explicitly preserves query fingerprint, ready/partial/stale quality, completeness, visible-row count, local data version and finite as-of time. An empty complete snapshot is authoritative empty while an incomplete empty snapshot is not treated as no suggestions configured.

The target read contract is synthetic and provider-free. It exposes immutable query results only and cannot become a mutation path; later import and writer slices separately own source normalization, durable commands and authorization.

This Phase 1 read boundary is executable only with deterministic provider-free evidence while the shipped app remains unchanged. It creates no default seed, mutation command, authorization policy, table, Sync Stream, provider choice, source transform, hosted resource or production authority.

items: VendorSuggestionID is a stable typed identity. VendorSuggestionDisplayValue trims surrounding whitespace, collapses internal whitespace for comparison, rejects empty/control/oversized values and preserves the accepted display spelling separately from its normalized lowercase comparison key.

VendorSuggestionSnapshot binds stable ID, AccountID, display value, active/archive lifecycle, unique UInt32 presentation order and UInt64 revision. Its selectable source value is only the display string; no Vendor, Item, Expense, Transaction, amount, category or relationship identity is present.

VendorSuggestionReferenceSnapshot rejects cross-Account rows, duplicate IDs, normalized values or presentation orders, mismatched visible counts and non-finite as-of evidence, then exposes deterministic order and active selectable entries without hiding archive state from the already-authorized snapshot.
VendorSuggestionQuerying exposes only watchVendorSuggestions(accountId:) and VendorSuggestionReferenceFailure supplies stable bounded value/scope/duplicate/count/time/local-read/encoding failures.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: This Phase 1 contract creates or changes no vendor_suggestions table, normalized key, order/revision/archive column, uniqueness rule, index, view, trigger or migration.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No SuggestVendor, rename, merge, archive, reactivate, reorder, default-seed, normalization-owner or authoritative read handler exists.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No relation, view or function is exposed through the Supabase Data API and no grant is added.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: Typed Account scope and an already-authorized local snapshot are not authorization proof. No membership, role, O-026 capability, grant, USING/WITH CHECK policy or cross-account database test exists.

syncStreams.notApplicable: No PowerSync Stream, local vendor-suggestion table, authenticated download predicate, upload connector, conflict handling or synchronized completeness proof is defined.

items: The complete snapshot is canonical Codable evidence over Account scope plus ListLocalSnapshot query fingerprint, rows, visible count, completeness, quality, version and finite as-of time; decode reconstructs through the same validators and byte-identical structured restart is required.

Ready, partial, stale and authoritative-empty states remain distinct. Duplicate stable identity, normalized value or order and cross-Account/count/time/malformed evidence fail atomically rather than being silently deduplicated or treated as ready.

A deterministic reference port may stream one exact synthetic Account snapshot or fail without yielding a false snapshot; this is not physical durable-store, process/device restart, authenticated Sync or provider evidence.

storageMedia.notApplicable: Vendor suggestions contain no attachment identity, local bytes, upload, cache, URL, retention or deletion behavior.

appMcp.notApplicable: No picker/settings UI, fixed/excluded option composition, free-text form control, save-as-suggestion capability gate, MCP resource/tool, transport handler or catalog registration is added.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No Firebase vendors array, hardcoded default, duplicate string, source order, Transaction/Item source, export record or production row is decoded, normalized, quarantined or reconciled.

observabilityRunbooks.notApplicable: Stable local failures are contract values only; no telemetry signal, metric, alert, audit sink or runbook action is introduced.

items: Implementation must remain inside provider-free LedgerTargetCore and tests and cannot change or link either application project.

The slice cannot authorize a reader or writer, seed defaults, mutate or persist suggestions, resolve O-026, create Vendor identity, change historical source text, define schema/RLS/Sync/provider/migration behavior, activate a feature, deploy, release or cut over.
A-003/A-004/A-007/A-016, physical offline verification, canonical production vendor-default profiling and all hosted-resource authority remain outside this read boundary.

verification.expected: Valid synthetic entries preserve exact stable ID, Account, display spelling, normalized comparison, lifecycle, order and revision; deterministic order and active selection yield only free-text source values and carry no Vendor/accounting identity, backend field or write capability.

Ready, partial, stale and authoritative-empty local snapshots round-trip byte-identically with exact query fingerprint, row order, visible count, completeness, quality, data version and finite as-of evidence.
Empty/control/oversized display values, cross-Account rows, duplicate IDs, normalized values or orders, count/time mismatches and malformed encodings fail atomically through stable diagnostic codes.
A deterministic provider-free reference port streams only its exact Account snapshot; a different Account and a failing port yield no false snapshot and return stable bounded failures.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: The exact implementation commit passes conversion traceability, provider/source-contamination and generated-contract checks, the complete target suite, both target builds and clean artifacts without changing an application project or claiming suggestion mutation, authentication, physical persistence, schema/RLS/Sync/provider, migration or production behavior.

notes: Ready decision-independent Phase 1 read boundary. Personal/current transaction and item source text plus reviewed capability/architecture contracts settle stable ordered Account-scoped suggestions, explicit archive/revision/readiness and the rule that selection remains free text rather than Vendor/accounting identity. O-026 remains fully open for suggestion creation, curation, archive/reactivation, merge, reorder and authorization. The slice stops before default policy, fixed/excluded picker composition, authentication, mutation, physical durability, schema/RLS/Sync/provider behavior, app/MCP, migration, hosted resources, production access or cutover.
